summary: Adds a discount_code field and an apply_discount method to Order. Adds order detail and discount redeem endpoints.

findings.title: Order detail readable by any logged-in user
findings.description: order_detail looks up the order by pk only and never filters on owner. The redeem view filters on owner=request.user, but order_detail does not. Any logged-in user can read another user's order total and discount code by changing the id in the URL. Add owner=request.user to the get_object_or_404 lookup, as redeem already does.

findings.consequence: Any logged-in user can read another user's order total and discount code by changing the id in the URL.
findings.fix: Add owner=request.user to the get_object_or_404 lookup, as redeem already does.

findings.title: Decimal multiplied by float raises TypeError
findings.description: Django loads total from the DecimalField as a Decimal. Python raises TypeError when apply_discount multiplies that Decimal by the float 0.9. Every redeem request with the valid code fails with a server error. No customer ever receives the discount. Multiply by Decimal("0.9") and quantize the result to two decimal places.

findings.consequence: Every redeem request with the valid code fails with a server error. No customer ever receives the discount.
findings.fix: Multiply by Decimal("0.9") and quantize the result to two decimal places.

findings.title: New model field has no migration
findings.description: The change adds discount_code to Order, but orders/migrations holds only 0001_initial. That migration has no discount_code column. Every Order query selects a column the database does not have, so order_list also fails. All order endpoints return server errors after deploy. Generate and commit a migration that adds discount_code to the orders table.

findings.consequence: Every Order query selects a column the database does not have, so order_list also fails. All order endpoints return server errors after deploy.
findings.fix: Generate and commit a migration that adds discount_code to the orders table.

findings.title: CSRF protection removed from a session-authenticated POST
findings.description: redeem changes order state and authenticates with the session cookie. The decorator turns off the CSRF check that the project's CsrfViewMiddleware would otherwise apply. Any third-party site can make a logged-in user's browser redeem codes on that user's orders. The impact is limited today because only one code is accepted. Remove the csrf_exempt decorator and send the CSRF token from the client.

findings.consequence: Any third-party site can make a logged-in user's browser redeem codes on that user's orders. The impact is limited today because only one code is accepted.
findings.fix: Remove the csrf_exempt decorator and send the CSRF token from the client.

findings.title: Once-per-order check is racy
findings.description: apply_discount checks discount_code on an in-memory copy, then saves without a lock. Two concurrent redeem requests can both pass the check. Concurrent requests can apply the discount twice to the same order. That breaks the once-per-order rule and loses the shop money. Lock the row with select_for_update inside a transaction. Another option is a conditional update filtered on discount_code being empty.

findings.fix: Lock the row with select_for_update inside a transaction. Another option is a conditional update filtered on discount_code being empty.

findings.title: New discount and endpoint behaviour has no covering test
findings.description: The repository has no tests for apply_discount, order_detail or redeem. Tests would have caught the float multiplication crash and the missing owner check before merge. Add tests for discount application, repeat redemption and access to another user's order.

findings.fix: Add tests for discount application, repeat redemption and access to another user's order.
